title: Deserts
source: After the notes' South America and Africa physical maps, with standard UPSC facts added

places.name: Atacama
places.significance: The driest desert on Earth, on Chile's Pacific coast, kept dry by the cold Peru current offshore
notes: In Chile
The driest desert in the world
Cold **Peruvian (Humboldt) current** offshore
Due to the easterly winds: they drop their rain east of the Andes and arrive dry

places.name: Patagonian Desert
places.significance: The rain-shadow desert of southern Argentina, in the lee of the Andes from the westerlies
notes: In Argentina
A rain shadow desert of the Andes
The **westerlies** drop their rain on the Chilean side
On the leeward side of the Andes

places.name: Sahara
places.significance: The largest hot desert on Earth, spanning North Africa from the Atlantic to the Red Sea
notes: The largest hot desert in the world, about 9 million km²
Its sandy part is the **erg**, its rocky plateau the **hamada**, its gravel plain the **serir** (reg)
The cold **Canary current** runs along its Atlantic coast
Its parts include the Libyan and Nubian deserts

places.name: Sahel
places.significance: The semi-arid belt along the great desert's southern edge, from Senegal to the Red Sea
notes: A semi-arid area, south of the Sahara
The **Great Green Wall** initiative: a belt of trees across Africa to hold back the desert
Prone to drought and desertification

places.name: Libyan Desert
places.significance: The great desert's dry north-eastern part, across three countries west of the river — mostly rock and gravel plain
notes: Mostly **serir** — a rocky, gravel plain
Covers eastern Libya, the Western Desert of Egypt and north-western Sudan
One of the driest parts of the Sahara

places.name: Nubian Desert
places.significance: The rocky desert of north-eastern Sudan, between the river's great bend and the Red Sea hills
notes: In Sudan, east of the Nile
Part of the Sahara: sandstone plateau and dry wadis

places.name: Namib
places.significance: The ancient coastal desert of south-west Africa, kept dry by the cold Benguela current offshore
notes: In Namibia (and southern Angola)
Cold **Benguela current** offshore
One of the oldest deserts on Earth, with some of its highest dunes

places.name: Kalahari
places.significance: The semi-arid sandy basin over most of Botswana, home of the San, the Bushmen
notes: Mainly in Botswana; also Namibia and South Africa
Home of the **Bushman** (San) tribe
A semi-desert: rain enough for grass and thorn scrub
